sections.title: What actually goes wrong
body: Watch enough sessions and the same failure modes repeat.
points: Edit before read: changing a file it has not looked at
Shallow analysis: a confident fix based on a skim
Spec deviation: quietly doing something other than the plan
Duplication: writing a new helper instead of finding the existing one
Context pressure: running out of room mid-task and losing the thread

sections.title: Each one is observable
body: An edit with no prior read is visible in the session. So is a pivot away from the stated plan, a compaction mid-task, or a jump in duplicated lines after a merge.

sections.title: Named, counted, shown back
body: Sensei tracks these as metrics, such as edit before read, spec deviation and context pressure, per repository, with the evidence behind each so you can judge it yourself.

sections.title: Prevent it, then catch what slips
body: Detection is the second line. Sensei’s workflow heads each pattern off before the work starts, its metrics catch what gets through, and the corrections you keep making become rules the assistant loads at the start of the next session.
points: Edit before read: the task is grounded first, in the spec and the code; edits made before any read are counted
Shallow analysis: the plan’s depth is checked before work starts, then an adversarial review hunts what was missed; retractions such as “I misread” are flagged
Spec deviation: scope and acceptance criteria are made explicit in the plan; a departure is shown as the plan quote against the action
Duplication: the code index is searched for an existing helper before a new one is written; duplication is measured at sampled commits
Context pressure: your rules are re-injected when the context compacts, and checkpoints let work resume; sessions that hit compaction are tracked

takeawaySub: Sensei heads them off, and shows you the evidence.
